chunks: He said, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) would supplicate during the recitation of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

O Allah! Our Lord, to You is the praise. You are the One Unified in Power and the Firm Authority, and to You is the praise. You are Exalted in Might and Greatness, above the heavens and the Great Throne. Our Lord.

And to You is the praise. You are the Self-Sufficient through Your Knowledge, and every possessor of knowledge is in need of You. Our Lord. And to You is the praise, O Revealer of the Verses and the Great Reminder. Our Lord, so to You is the praise for what You taught us of Wisdom and the Great, Clear Quran.
O Allah, You taught it to us before our desire to learn it, and You singled us out for it before our desire to benefit from it.
O Allah, since that was a favor from You, a grace, generosity, and kindness to us, and mercy for us, and gratitude upon us, without any effort or power or strength on our part.

O Allah, then make beautiful to us its fine recitation, and the memorization of its verses, and faith in its allegorical parts, and action upon its decisive parts, and a means in its interpretation, and guidance in its arrangement, and insight into its light.
O Allah, and as You revealed it as a healing for Your friends, and a misery for Your enemies, and a blindness upon the people of Your disobedience, and a light for the people of Your obedience.

O Allah, then make it for us a fortress from Your punishment and a protection from Your wrath, and a barrier from Your disobedience, and a preservation from Your anger, and a pointer towards Your obedience, and a light on the Day we meet You by which we shine among Your creation, and by which we cross upon Your Path, and by which we are guided to Your Paradise.
O Allah, we seek refuge in You from misfortune in bearing it, and blindness from acting upon it, and tyranny in its judgment, and arrogance regarding its intent, and deficiency below its due right.
O Allah, carry for us its weight, and obligate for us its reward, and grant us its gratitude, and make us to observe it and preserve it.
O Allah, make us follow its permissible, and avoid its prohibitions, and establish its limits, and fulfill its obligations.
O Allah, grant us sweetness in its recitation, and vigor in its recitation, and awe in its slow recitation, and strength in its application during the nights and the ends of the day.

O Allah, and cure us from sleep with a little, and wake us during a time of the night from the sleep of the sleepers, and rouse us at the times when supplication is answered, from the slumber of the slumberers.
O Allah, make for our hearts intelligence regarding its wonders that do not expire, and delight in its repetition, and a lesson in its returning, and clear benefit in its understanding.

O Allah, we seek refuge in You from its lagging in our hearts, and its being a pillow during our sleep, and its being thrown behind our backs, and we seek refuge in You from the hardness of our hearts to what it admonished us with.

O Allah, benefit us with what You directed in it from the verses, and remind us with what You struck in it from the parables, and expiate from us the evil deeds through its interpretation, and multiply for us through it the reward for the good deeds, and raise us through it in reward in the ranks, and teach us the glad tidings through it after death.

O Allah, make it for us provision by which we are strengthened in the standing before You, and a clear path by which we travel to You, and beneficial knowledge by which we thank Your bounties, and true humility by which we glorify Your names.
For indeed You have taken it as a proof upon us, cut off our excuse by it, and created for us a favor through it for which our gratitude fell short.

O Allah, make it for us a friend that confirms us from slipping, and a pointer that guides us to the righteous deed, and an aiding guide that corrects us from deviation, and an aid that strengthens us from fatigue, until it reaches us to the best of hopes.

O Allah, make it for us an intercessor on the Day of Meeting, and a weapon on the Day of Ascension, and an argument on the Day of Judgment, and a light on the Day of Darkness, the Day when there is no earth and no sky, the Day when every striver is recompensed for what he strove for.
O Allah, make it for us a drink on the Day of Thirst, and success on the Day of Recompense from the Blazing Fire, of little survival for those who are scorched in it, and blaze with its heat.
O Allah, make it for us a proof against the chiefs of the nations on the Day when the people of the earth and the people of the sky are gathered.
O Allah, grant us the stations of the martyrs, and the life of the happy, and the companionship of the Prophets. Indeed, You are the Hearer of the supplication.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited during Quran recitation according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this supplication reflects the Imami tradition of viewing the Quran not merely as a text to be recited, but as a living entity (*wali*) that requires spiritual guardianship and active implementation. It emphasizes the dual nature of the Quran as both a source of healing for the faithful and a means of distinction on the Day of Judgment, while seeking protection from the specific spiritual dangers of neglect and superficial engagement.
